lessons.title: Array Basics
lessons.concept: An array stores values in contiguous memory locations for fast direct index access. Access is O(1); search/insert/delete are O(n) unless at the end.
lessons.worked_example: arr = [10, 20, 30]. arr[1] = 20 in O(1). Insert at index 0 requires shifting all elements → O(n).
mistakes: Confusing array access O(1) with search O(n)
Forgetting arrays are fixed-size in many languages

lessons.title: Array Traversal
lessons.concept: Visit each element once using a loop. Time O(n), space O(1). Use for finding max, sum, search.
lessons.worked_example: Find max: initialize max = arr[0]; loop i=1..n-1; if arr[i] > max, max = arr[i].

practice.question: Time complexity of accessing an element in an array?
practice.explanation: Arrays support direct index access → O(1).

practice.question: Which is NOT a linear data structure?
practice.explanation: Tree is non-linear (hierarchical). Array, linked list, queue are linear.

questions.question: What does this do for array arr of size n? for(i=0;i<n;i++) arr[i]=i;
questions.explanation: Each element arr[i] is set to its own index i.

questions.question: Best for implementing back functionality in a web browser?
questions.explanation: Back uses LIFO (last visited page first) → stack.

questions.question: Stable sorting algorithm?
questions.explanation: Merge sort is stable (preserves relative order of equal elements).
